_schema: Generated by render_actions.js from ACTIONS.json — do not hand-edit. One row per action: [id, surface]. The agent-facing table of contents: hold this in context, fetch full entries by id via tools/session/actions_query.js. No urgency/importance here — the live AI scores those at decision time.

Three road-tier rows (Track / Road / Highway) at the bottom of the tile construction ledger, below the building candidates - plus the Planetary canvas, which is the second half of the control: the row ARMS and the canvas is where the crossing is aimed (BL-1370; docs/ui/ledgers/construction.md 'A road is built from a road to a tile, in two presses').

The command seam only (--serve / MCP `issue_command` with `nation`, and the verify API's `corp_command{as_nation=...}`). No ledger or card control yet: a state building's card names its nation as owner ("Owner: <nation> (state industry)") and offers no levers.

Select a tile (Planetary canvas click), then Construction ledger > Construction view > the tile's building list > road ladder (after Highway) > 'Track' row > 'Build'. NO ARMED TOOL, and that is a real difference from the ROAD rows it sits under: a road is a crossing between two tiles and so arms and is then aimed at a neighbour (BL-1370, gameplay.place_road), while rail track is laid ON a tile and names no side at all (LOGISTICS.md 4c) - so this press builds where the road presses arm. Also the command seam (--serve / MCP `issue_command` verb `lay_track` with `nation`; the verify API's `corp_command{verb=lay_track, as_nation=...}`).

The nation selection screen at Begin (STARTUP.md § The seat; Ben, 2026-10-10): the list of the MAJOR nations only (a nation holding a champion; majors and seats are one-to-one, so the rows are the major target's count) beside a map of the home body, the seven-part nation card (territory lit on the map, population and GDP, treasury and budget weights, resource profile and deposits, neighbours with their reading and grudges, and history: pattern tags, a short timeline, and a link into the History ledger filtered to the nation), a nation's briefing, and its Confirm press. The ONE pre-play entry in this dictionary: the wizard's rounds have none (NR-804), but the pick is a game act (Ben, 2026-09-24) - it decides which nation the player IS - so an agent must be able to make it. It is a corp_verb (29) sent AS THE NATION (corp == as_nation == the nation), but the seat is taken ONCE, BEFORE PLAY: the in-play agent hosts (--serve's COMMAND and the live --host-agent seam) refuse it with rejected_state, and an agent makes the pick at launch with `--seat <nation-id>` (every new-campaign path, --autostart included). The screen is shaped for up to six humans and seats one (NR-1025). NOTE FOR A PLANNER: the list order is the majors' static landscape score (the ground the nation's own buildings stand on), and a major below the viability floor is MARKED but offered; a marked major is a harder opening, never an illegal one. BL-1406: the list shows NATIONS - name (marked 'below the floor' where the viability floor marked it) and treasury; the Champion and Industry columns and the card's champion section retired with the champion (STARTUP.md § The seat).

The research panel's ring: SHIFT + left click on a node (Ben, 2026-10-10; there is no Plan mode - a plain click or a hover only inspects). A corp_verb (33, `queue_research`), so an agent issues it through the same seam.
The research panel: SHIFT + left click on a QUEUED node (the toggle rule, NR-1033), or the 'Remove last' button under the queue. A corp_verb (34, `unqueue_research`).
The research panel's column: the 'Clear' button under the queue (always shown while the seat's nation exists). A corp_verb (35, `clear_research`).

Command line. One of the two routes into spectator mode for a human, both at the start of a session; the other is the nation selection screen's Spectate press (chrome.seat_spectate). Before BL-695 the mode was reachable solely from `verify.spectate()` behind --verify, i.e. it was a headless-script capability and not something a person could do.

Command line, no window. Dispatched before any SDL window, renderer or ImGui context exists, like --serve and --export-blackboard.
Command line. The only route to a start other than the default 1960 one (BL-705 opened the flag; epoch 0 is retired, NR-920).
